subject: Clarifying carveout scope: punitive/incidental/consequential — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MSA – damages carveouts (redlines)

Diego —

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal team pushed back on the damages section and proposed a one-way exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages in favor of the customer. Their concern is to preserve recoverability for lost profits and downstream customer claims tied to our service. I've attached our annotated MSA and a short summary of the positions.

Key asks from Acme:
- Keep consequential and special damages excluded from Redwood liability, but preserve carveouts for (i) breach of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) willful misconduct, and (iv) aggregated third-party claims tied to data handling.
- Remove mutuality language; the exclusion should read one-way (Redwood limited).

We understand this is non-standard for many SaaS vendors; happy to take a call to walk through the risks. Do you have an initial read?

Thanks,
Sara Hughes
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_Annotated_MSA_redlines.pdf (14 pages)
Attachment: redline_summary.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA – damages carveouts (redlines)

Sara —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the summary. Looping in our in-house counsel (Laura) and commercial (Markus, Marissa) to get aligned internally. Quick initial thoughts:

- One-way exclusions usually set a tough precedent for renewals and enterprise procurement teams. We try to avoid asymmetry except in very large, strategic deals.
- That said, we are open to narrowing the definition of "consequential" and carving out a short list of exceptions that matter to you (IP, confidentiality, willful misconduct, and certain data-related third-party claims).

To speed this along, Laura — can you do a two-option proposal (aggressive mutual exclusion v. customer-favored one-way with stronger carveouts) that we can present to Acme as options? We'd like snippets we can drop into their redline. I'll also propose a short 30-min call tomorrow to run through tradeoffs.

Sara — would tomorrow at 10:00 PT work for you?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA – damages carveouts (redlines)

Team —

Attached are two redline snippets and a one-page rationale (see Proposed_Carveout_Snippets.docx). Summary here so Diego can share:

Option A (Preferred from legal/commercial alignment):
- Mutual exclusion of Consequential, Incidental, Special and Punitive damages for both parties, except for the following express carveouts where liability remains: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) indemnifiable IP infringement; (c) willful misconduct; (d) claims arising from Redwood's negligent handling of customer data leading to third-party claims.
- Preserve Order Form caps and direct-damage recovery; do not expand to include lost profits in those exceptions.

Option B (Customer-favored compromise):
- One-way exclusion drafted in favor of the customer, but with narrower definition of "consequential" and explicit examples that exclude purely speculative downstream economic loss. Include an escalation mechanic: if the customer's redline is accepted, apply a stricter security covenant (SOC 2 plus annual pen test) and a modest reduction in the per-token pricing to compensate.

Legal analysis / risks:
- One-way exclusions shift negotiation leverage on later renewals and create internal precedence risk. They also expose Redwood to unpredictable high-severity claims if we accept broad customer-side carveouts without reciprocal protections.
- A mutual exclusion with the carveouts listed above strikes the best balance of limiting systemic exposure while addressing Acme's specific concerns.

Snippets (short form to paste in redline):

"Consequential Damages Exclusion — Legal Snippet (Mutual)"
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, consequential, special, incidental, exemplary or punitive damages, including without limitation loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of customers; provided, however, that the foregoing shall not apply to (i) a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations; (ii) claims for indemnifiable infringement of intellectual property; (iii) willful misconduct; and (iv) third-party claims arising from a party's negligent or intentional mishandling of the other party's data."

"Consequential Damages Exclusion — Legal Snippet (One-way, limited)"
"Without limiting any other remedy, Redwood shall not be liable for indirect, consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, including lost profits; provided that Redwood's liability shall remain for (i) breach of confidentiality; (ii) indemnifiable third-party IP claims; (iii) willful misconduct; and (iv) material mishandling of Customer Data that gives rise to third-party claims. Acceptance of this one-way exclusion by Redwood will be conditioned on (a) Customer's execution of the attached Security Rider, and (b) mutual agreement on a price concession reflected in the Order Form."

Next steps:
1) Diego — decide whether to present Option A + B as alternatives or push for A only.
2) If customer insists on one-way language, obtain commercial approval and security rider sign-off (Markus).

Attachment: Proposed_Carveout_Snippets.docx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA – damages carveouts (redlines)

Diego / Laura —

Commercial view: strong preference for Option A (mutual exclusion with limited carveouts). We do not want to set a precedent where sales teams accept asymmetric carveouts without a clear, documented business case. That said, if Acme is strategic (they are), we can consider Option B but only with the following commercial guardrails:

- Require a signed Security Rider and annual attestations (SOC 2 + pen test).
- Attach a modest one-time credit (not recurring) and a 12-month price hold to offset incremental risk.
- Escalation: any customer-side precedent must be reviewed by Sales Leadership and Legal Ops and captured in a central exceptions register.

If Diego thinks the deal stalls without one-way language, we can present both options to Acme and offer the customer the limited one-way language only after they sign the Security Rider and accept the pricing concession.

Markus
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

2) If Acme cannot accept mutuality, we will consider a conditional one-way exclusion (your requested posture) provided we execute a Security Rider (SOC 2 + annual pen test) and a small, one-time commercial concession.

If you're available, let's take 30 minutes on Monday morning (11/16) to go through both options; otherwise, you're welcome to accept Option A language as-is to speed execution.
